scope: Remaining FOR-45 gaps: the GitHub Issues source and its label, assignee, milestone and state filters are per project, driven by the project's FOR-47 confirmed ticket source; schema 34 migrates the former workspace-level source into the projects that use it; live import repeated at the final revision with two pages and a closed-issue state change.

simulated.provider: Loopback GitHub API fixtures (axum in crates/crewroom-service/tests/github_issues.rs; std TcpListener in crates/crewroom-desktop/src/workbench/github_issues_tests.rs) and core/runtime store tests; not github.com.
checks: Core: a project without a confirmed GitHub source cannot save filters, labels or commit a sync; confirming GitHub Issues starts the project with state open and no labels; the repository comes from the confirmed source and a repository key in the filters is refused

Core: two projects keep separate filters and sync results; re-confirming the same repository keeps filters and the last sync; confirming Jira removes the project's GitHub sync; confirming another repository starts over and a sync of the replaced source is refused
Core: a ticket first imported by a project's sync targets that project (repositoryId); identity matching, re-acceptance, failures and unreadable issues behave as before

Core: schema 34 copies a schema-33 workspace-level source (filters, milestone, workflow labels, last sync) into the project whose confirmed source is the same repository (case-insensitive), starts other confirmed GitHub projects with open issues only, leaves unconfirmed projects without a sync, and removes the adopted record; an unused one is kept and adopted by the next project that confirms its repository

Service: /api/repositories/{id}/github-issues/{filters|labels|sync}; sync and filters are refused (409) before confirmation; filters reach GitHub; two pages, PR exclusion, re-sync re-acceptance, rate limit, no access and issues disabled (each in its own project, leaving the first project's last sync intact), revoked token, close/reopen re-read, gone issues and secondary rate limit; workspace githubIssues lists each project by id and name and reports an unadopted workspace-level source
Runtime: issue delivery resolves the source and workflow labels per ticket from the project whose confirmed repository serves it

Desktop: Settings → Repositories confirms the suggested GitHub source, shows the project's not-synced state and default filters, saves filters and workflow labels, states the missing connection, syncs after connecting, and Settings → Integrations names the project beside its status; imported tickets show GitHub open/closed and target the project

live.endpoint: https://api.github.com through a debug crewroomd built from 6a0a65d (sha256 aa9840e8840b4b7da24cb9087e1071e852a88f0c4cf88f01a45b90fff9c4c29b), loopback port 4391, isolated --data-dir in an ignored worktree path (deleted afterwards)
live.repository: Operator-approved private sandbox <owner>/crewroom-e2e-sandbox. 101 synthetic issues #10-#110 titled 'FOR-45 synthetic page issue NNN' with label for-45-pages were created for this run and closed as not planned afterwards; #10 was closed during the run to observe the state change.
live.project: A local Git checkout whose origin is git@github.com:<owner>/crewroom-e2e-sandbox.git (never fetched), linked as project 'Sandbox'.
live.credential: CREWROOM_GITHUB_TOKEN set from the operator's gh CLI login in the daemon environment only; never printed. It is a gh OAuth token, not a fine-grained or classic PAT.
live.pagination: The client requests per_page=100; 101 matching issues therefore needed a second page through Link rel=next. Individual page requests were not logged; the count proves that more than one page was read.
live.observation: Immediately after #10 was closed, GitHub's state=open listing still returned it (with state closed in the payload), so that sync counted 101 matching issues; the next state=open sync listed 100 and re-read #10 as closed.
live.redaction: Repository owner replaced with <owner>. No token is retained.
